Yujin Han, Sung Woo Joo, Hangsik Shin, "Evaluating Feature Selection Methods for Radiomic Tractometry in
Schizophrenia." Scheduled for presentation on Thursday July 17, 2025, 13:30-15:30 hrs.

Abstract— This study investigates the optimal feature 
selection technique in brain radiomic tractometry for 
schizophrenia discrimination. Features were selected using 
point-biserial correlation, Cohen's d, and mutual information, 
and classification performance was evaluated using an 
XGBoost model. Combining mutual information and 
point-biserial correlation improves classification performance 
and reduces overfitting. 
Clinical Relevance — This study enhances the utility of 
radiomic tractometry in neuroimaging studies. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Radiomic tractometry analyzes microstructural changes in 
white matter tracts by extracting quantitative features from 
medical imaging [1]. However, radiomic features consist of 
high-dimensional data, making direct analysis challenging. 
Therefore, feature selection is essential to identify 
meaningful information and reduce noise. Despite its 
importance, the optimal method remains undefined, resulting 
in a variety of approaches [2]. Therefore, this study aims to 
compare feature selection methods for radiomic tractometry 
analysis and propose improvements. We evaluate and 
compare the performance of machine learning models in 
schizophrenia classification using radiomic features from 
schizophrenia patients and healthy controls, based on 
different feature selection methods. 
II. METHODS 
The dataset was retrospectively collected from Asan 
Medical Center (Seoul, South Korea) after institutional 
review board approval (IRB No. 2021 -1128), and includes 
brain MRI voxel data from schizophrenia patients (n=124; 
male: 44%; age range: 19 –66) and healthy controls (n=77; 
male: 31%; age range: 21 –52). A total of 58,380 radiomic 
features were extracted using the Python library pyradiomics 
[3]. Batch effects from scanner differences were harmonized 
using the Combat algorithm [4]. 
Feature selection methods applied were point -biserial 
correlation (PBC), Cohen's d (CD), and mutual information 
(MI), evaluating correlation with the target variable, group 
mean differences, and nonlin ear associations, respectively. 
Cut-off values for PBC and CD were set at weak (0.25) and 
moderate (0.5) thresholds. For MI, the optimal number of

Additionally, the performance of models based on feature 
intersections was analyzed. XGBoost was used for 
classification, and the final model was evaluated on a 
separate test dataset, optimized using Bayesian optimization. 
III. RESULTS 
Table 1 presents the number of selected features and the 
classification performance of each method. Among single 
methods, MI achieved the highest test AUC (0.83). 
Combining methods reduced overfitting, with MI ∩PBC 
yielding the highest test AUC (0.85) despite selecting only 29 
features. The features selected by PBC were entirely 
contained within those selected by CD, resulting in identical 
outcomes for PBC and PBC∩CD. Similarly, PBC∩MI and 
PBC∩CD∩MI produced identical results. 
IV. DISCUSSION & CONCLUSION 
This study demonstrated that combining MI and PBC in 
feature selection effectively captures the complex structure of 
white matter and the nonlinear characteristics of radiomics 
data, achieving the best classification performance. These 
results demonstrate that the combination of MI and PBC is an 
effective strategy for selecting important information in 
high-dimensional radiomics data.
